nodes.title: SG-7.10 Claude Code CLI adapter with restricted permissions and no raw community text
nodes.body:
Context: backend/worker/internal/provider/claude.go already has a Claude adapter that calls an Exec interface with `claude -p <fixed prompt>`, with unit tests using a recording fake Exec. It passes no permission restrictions. Desired behavior: the adapter limits what the CLI may do, never uses a shell, and receives only a constant instruction that points at structured tasks under development/tasks, never raw community text. Expected result: unit tests with a fake Exec prove all of this. Why: community prompts are untrusted and the coding agent must run restricted.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the Claude adapter, when Run is called, then the Exec receives permission-restricting flags that exclude shell and network tools
- Given the Claude adapter, when Run is called, then the args contain only a fixed prompt naming development/tasks and no caller-supplied text
- Given an empty work directory, when Run is called, then it returns an error and Exec is not called


## Scope
- In scope: backend/worker/internal/provider/claude.go
- In scope: backend/worker/internal/provider/claude_test.go
- Out of scope: Real command executor implementation
- Out of scope: Runner changes
- Out of scope: Mock provider
- Preserve: Exec interface signature
- Preserve: NewClaude nil-Exec error
- Preserve: Cost 0 return and error wrapping with the 'provider claude' prefix
- Preserve: provider.New factory behavior


## Technical constraints
- No shell: command name and args are passed to Exec as a list
- Tests use a fake Exec only


## Definition of done
- Adapter restricted and unit tests pass with go test ./internal/provider


## Non-functional requirements
- Security: untrusted community text never reaches the agent command line


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Claude adapter passes restricted-permission flags to the CLI
nodes.body:
Context: Claude.Run currently calls Exec with only `-p` and the prompt. Desired behavior: also pass `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, `--allowedTools Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep` and `--disallowedTools Bash,WebFetch,WebSearch`. Expected result: the agent can edit workspace files but not run shell commands or reach the network. Why: restricted permissions are mandated for coding agents.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a fake Exec, when Run is called, then args contain --permission-mode followed by acceptEdits
- Given a fake Exec, when Run is called, then --disallowedTools lists Bash and --allowedTools does not list Bash


## Scope
- In scope: Argument list built in Claude.Run
- Out of scope: Executor implementation
- Preserve: Exec interface
- Preserve: Run return values


## Technical constraints
- Args are a []string, never a joined command string


## Definition of done
- Flags present in args


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Claude adapter accepts only structured input and rejects an empty work directory
nodes.body:
Context: claudePrompt is a constant but Run does not validate workDir. Desired behavior: Run returns an error containing 'work dir' when workDir is empty or whitespace, without calling Exec; the prompt arg remains exactly claudePrompt. Expected result: no caller-controlled text can enter the command line and the CLI never runs in an unspecified directory. Why: untrusted-input and workspace isolation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given workDir is empty, when Run is called, then it returns an error mentioning work dir and Exec is not called
- Given a valid workDir, when Run is called, then the argument after -p equals the fixed prompt and the args contain no workDir text


## Scope
- In scope: Claude.Run validation and prompt use
- Out of scope: Requirement file generation
- Preserve: Error wrapping of Exec failures


## Technical constraints
- No new Run parameters; Agent interface unchanged


## Definition of done
- Validation and fixed prompt covered


## Clarifying questions
- None
